rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a Day-5 blastocyst and the reported 2AB, but it overstates quality as 'high-quality/good-to-strong' and describes the TE as relatively cohesive despite the image/lab grade suggesting sparse, loose TE. It also infers symmetry and absence of debris more confidently than a single static image supports.

Integrates most relevant factors well: age 33, prior live birth, male factor diagnosis, endometrial thickness, BMI, FSH, and untested status. It appropriately links these to prognosis, though AMH is unavailable and some factors like former smoking/stress may be weighted a bit heavily.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with prognosis derived from embryo grade plus patient context. Minor issues include some overoptimistic wording relative to a 2AB embryo and slight overemphasis on weaker predictors such as former smoking and stress.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based: single embryo transfer, luteal support per protocol, no bed rest, avoid routine add-ons, selective rather than automatic PGT-A at age 33, and further workup only if repeated failures occur. Small deviations include speculative comments about lingering former smoking effects on receptivity.

Provides practical next steps for transfer management and future planning, including SET, medication adherence, follow-up, lifestyle optimization, and when to consider further male-factor or uterine evaluation. Useful and clinically oriented, though not highly individualized beyond standard recommendations.
